title: The Morning Run
story: Jonas had promised himself a morning run three days a week. On Thursday he woke before the alarm and tied his trainers. The street was quiet, and the air felt cool on his face. He did a short stretch by the park gate. Then he set off along his usual route around the lake. He kept an easy pace and did not race the cyclists. At first he could breathe without effort. After one lap his chest felt tighter. He slowed down, shook his arms, and drank from his bottle. The tight feeling passed, and his steps grew even again. His friend Yusuf waved from a bench. Jonas lifted a hand but did not stop to talk. He wanted to finish the route he had planned. Near the bridge he looked at his watch. He had been moving for twenty minutes. His knees felt fine, and his breathing was steady. A thought about a college test came into his head. He let the thought go and watched the water instead. The run was for a clear head, not for worry. On the last street he kept that easy pace and stopped at his door. He walked slowly for two minutes so his heart could settle. His face was warm, and his shirt was damp, but he felt proud. Inside he drank water and ate a banana. He wrote the time in a notebook beside his bed.
